p2.original: 人类的记忆是一种信息加工系统，它会对信息进行建设性的编码、存储和提取。
p2.en: Human memory is an information-processing system that is constructive in coding, storing and extracting information.

p3.original: 毋庸置疑，记忆确实会对我们耍花招。我们防御这些花招的最好方法就是理解记忆是如何工作的。因此，让我们从记忆的定义开始建立对它的理解：认知心理学家把记忆（memory）视为一个编码、存储和提取信息的系统。顺便说一下，这个定义同样适用于有生命的生物体及计算机。然而，与计算机的记忆不同的是，人类的认知记忆系统选择性地，有时是带有偏见地，从感官中获取信息，并将其转换成有意义的模式加以存储，之后根据需要对这些模式进行提取。这样，这些记忆模式就成了人们思维和行为的原料，进而使你能够认出朋友的脸、会骑自行车、回忆起去迪士尼乐园的旅行，以及（如果一切顺利的话）在考试中回忆起你需要用到的概念。更普遍而言，这一学习阶段的核心概念可以采用以下语言来定义记忆：
p3.en: There's no doubt that memory does play tricks on us. The best way to defend ourselves against these manoeuvres is to understand how memory works. So let's start with the definition of memory and build an understanding of it: cognitive psychologists see memory as a system of coding, storing and extracting information. By the way, this definition applies equally to living organisms and computers. However, unlike computer memory, human cognitive memory systems selectively, sometimes biasedly, capture information from senses and convert it into meaningful models for storage, which are then extracted as needed. In this way, these patterns of memory become a source of thought and behavior, which in turn enables you to recognize the face of a friend, to ride a bicycle, to recall the trip to Disneyland, and, if everything goes well, to recall in the examination the concept that you need to use. More generally, the core concept of this learning stage can be defined in the following languages:

p4.original: 人类的记忆是一种信息加工系统，它会对信息进行建设性的编码、存储和提取。
p4.en: Human memory is an information-processing system that is constructive in coding, storing and extracting information.

p5.original: 首先，请大家注意核心概念中的“建设性”一词。虽然我们经常用这个词来暗示某些事情是有益的（如“建设性的批评意见”），但我们在此处提到的记忆的建设性却有不同的含义。从这个意义上说，我们是用建设性来指代我们记忆系统的真实的建构过程。也就是说，我们不会以一种静态的、可预测的方式接收和存储信息。正如你所看到的，当我们学习记忆的基础知识时，我们对信息和事件的独特的、个人化的解释改变了我们编码和记住它们的方式，这解释了身处同一情境中的人们如何以不同的方式记住这一情境。让我们通过观察人们通常（但错误地）用来描述记忆的隐喻来更详细地审视这个观点。
p5.en: First, attention is drawn to the term “constructive” in the core concept. While we often use this term to suggest that certain things are useful (such as “constructive criticism”), the constructiveness of the memories we have mentioned here has different meanings. In that sense, we are constructively pointing to the true construction of our memory system. In other words, we will not receive and store information in a static and predictable manner. As you can see, when we learn the basics of memory, our unique, personal interpretation of information and events changes the way we code and remember them, which explains how people in the same situation remember this situation in different ways. Let us look at this in greater detail by observing the metaphors that people usually (but wrongly) use to describe memory.

p7.original: 5.1 认识到记忆代表我们对事件的独特感知，它既不准确也不客观。
p7.en: 5.1 Recognizing that memory represents our unique perception of events, it is neither accurate nor objective.

p8.original: 5.1 记忆是被建构和重构的

p10.original: 认识到记忆代表我们对事件的独特感知，它既不准确也不客观。
p10.en: Recognizing that memory represents our unique perception of events, it is neither accurate nor objective.

p11.original: 我们经常借用隐喻来理解复杂的观点。有一种隐喻是将人类的记忆类比为图书馆或仓库，这种隐喻强调记忆具有存储大量信息的能力（Haberlandt，1999）。另一种隐喻则把记忆类比为计算机。但是，一些关于记忆的隐喻是有误导性的。例如，将记忆类比为“录像机”的隐喻就存在误导性，这个隐喻意味着人类的记忆能够完整而准确地记录一切经历。
p11.en: We often use metaphors to understand complex points of view. There is a metaphor for the analogy of human memory as a library or warehouse, which emphasizes the ability of memory to store large amounts of information (Haberlandt, 1999). Another metaphor compares memories to computers. However, some metaphors of memory are misleading. For example, the metaphor of the analogy of memory as a “video recorder” is misleading and implies that human memory can record all experiences in a complete and accurate manner.

p12.original: 实验结果清楚地表明了这种“录像机”隐喻是错误的。尤其是在一些“恢复记忆”的案例中，相信记忆具有永久的准确性是危险的。事实上，人类的记忆是一个解释系统，它像艺术家一样，在接收信息时会抛弃某些细节部分，然后将剩余的信息组织成有意义的模式。因此，我们的记忆代表了我们对事件的独特知觉（perception），而不是对事件本身准确或客观的表征。
p12.en: The results clearly demonstrate that this “video recorder” metaphor is wrong. Particularly in some cases of “restoration of memory”, it is dangerous to believe that memory is permanently accurate. In fact, human memory is an interpretation system that, like an artist, discards certain details when receiving information and then organizes the remaining information into meaningful models. Our memory therefore represents our unique perception of events, rather than an accurate or objective representation of the events themselves.

p13.original: 简单来说，我们并未在严格意义上提取记忆，事实上我们重构了它们。我们首先搜寻记忆的碎片，这些碎片类似于拼图游戏中的碎片。然后，从这些碎片中，我们根据我们记忆中的样子，而不是根据实际情况，填充其中的空白部分以重构事件（或想法、情感和图像）。在大多数情况下，这种方法很有效，以至于你根本没有意识到你的记忆有多少实际上是猜测的！
p13.en: In short, we have not taken memories in the strict sense of the word, and we have in fact recreated them. We start by searching for fragments of memory, which are similar to those in puzzle games. Then, from these fragments, we recreate events (or ideas, emotions and images) by filling out the blanks in them, based on what we remember, rather than what we actually see. In most cases, this method works so well that you don't realize how much of your memory is actually guessed!

p14.original: 看看图5-1的内容应该会让你相信记忆存在这种重构过程。
p14.en: Looking at the contents of figure 5-1 should convince you that there is such a re-engineering process in memory.

p16.original: 注：哪张图片准确地描绘了1美分硬币？
p16.en: Note: Which picture accurately depicts a dollar coin?

p17.original: 想一想，除非你是一名硬币收藏家，否则你可能很难注意到这类熟悉的物品的细节。因此，在提取一美分硬币的图像时，你会在脑海中自动填充空白及缺少的细节，而不会意识到自己实际上创造了多少记忆图像。正确答案是A。
p17.en: Think about it, unless you're a coin collector, you might find it difficult to notice the details of these familiar items. So, when you take a dollar coin, you automatically fill your head with blanks and missing details, without realizing how much memory you actually create. The correct answer is A.

p18.original: 相较于其他记忆，有些记忆更粗糙。心理学家发现，我们一般对下列信息的记忆是最完整和最准确的：
p18.en: Some memories are rougher than others. Psychologists have found that our memories of the following information are generally the most complete and accurate:

p19.original: 我们集中注意在自己予以关注的信息上，例如，在其他谈话背景下关注某个朋友的话语；
p19.en: We focus on the information we are concerned with, for example, in the context of other conversations, on the words of a friend;

p20.original: 我们感兴趣的信息，如最喜欢的电影里的情节；
p20.en: Information of interest to us, such as the scenes of the favorite film;

p21.original: 能够使我们的情绪唤起的信息，如特别愉快或痛苦的经历（但是如果这些信息也同时附带着偏见，就像当我们与所爱之人进行激烈争论时那样，那么这种使我们情绪唤起的信息便无法被完整和准确地记住）；
p21.en: (a) A message that can make our emotions feel, such as a particularly pleasant or painful experience (but if it is accompanied by prejudice, as when we have a violent argument with the person we love, then the message that makes us emotional cannot be remembered in its entirety and accurately);

p22.original: 与以前的经历有关的信息，如与你上周参加的音乐会中做表演的那名音乐家有关的一条新闻；
p22.en: Information about previous experiences, such as a story about the musician who performed at the concert you attended last week;

p23.original: 我们复述过的信息，如考试前复习的材料。
p23.en: We repeat information, such as pre-test review material.

p24.original: 本章的后续部分将展开介绍这种记忆的认知取向，即信息加工模型（information-processing model）。该模型强调信息在成为永久性记忆的过程中所经历的系统性变化——与简单的录像机模型截然不同。信息加工模型也强调记忆的功能性，也就是说，它为我们行使有用的功能。我们稍后会了解到，记忆最基本的功能就是信息的编码、存储和提取。
p24.en: The following section of this chapter will introduce the cognitive orientation of this memory, i.e. the information-processing model. The model emphasizes the systemic changes that information has undergone in becoming permanent memory - distinct from simple video recorder models. The information processing model also emphasizes the functionality of memory, that is, it performs useful functions for us. We will learn later that the most basic function of memory is the coding, storage and extraction of information.

p26.original: 简单来说，人类的记忆将本质上无意义的感觉信息（如老师的声音）转化为有意义的模式（词汇、句子和概念），并且之后你可以对其进行存储和使用。要做到这一点，记忆必须先将传入的感觉信息编码成一种有效的格式。
p26.en: In short, human memory translates essentially meaningless sensory information (e.g. the teacher's voice) into meaningful models (nouns, sentences and concepts) and you can store and use it later. To do this, memory must first encode the incoming sensory information into a valid format.

p27.original: 1. 编码（encoding）首先需要你从大量的感觉输入中选择某一刺激事件，并对这个刺激进行初步分类。它是声音、图像、气味、味道或者疼痛？接下来，你需要识别这个输入刺激的独特特征。如果它是一种声音，那它是响亮的、轻柔的，还是刺耳的？它是否符合某种模式，如汽车喇叭、一段旋律或是人的嗓音？它是你以前听过的声音吗？最后，你会在心里给这个声音贴上标签，使之变得有意义。（“这个声音是约翰逊博士的，他是我的心理学教授！”）
p27.en: 1. The encoding requires first that you select an incentive event from a large amount of sensory input and make a preliminary classification of the stimulus. Is it sound, image, smell, smell or pain? Next, you need to identify the unique characteristics of this input stimulus. If it's a sound, then it's loud, soft, or hard-eared? Is it in line with some pattern, like car horns, a melody or a human voice? Is it a voice you've heard before? And finally, you'll label this voice in your heart and make it meaningful. "This voice belongs to Dr. Johnson, my professor of psychology! The blogger says:

p28.original: 一方面，编码是如此自动和快速，以至于我们无法意识到这一过程。例如，尽管你没有刻意地将吃早餐的经历牢牢地“印”在你的脑海中，你也可能会回忆起今天早上吃了什么。情绪化的经历更可能在没有努力编码的情况下留在记忆中（Dolan，2002），如与同事之间的一次愤怒的争吵。
p28.en: On the one hand, the code is so automatic and so fast that we cannot be aware of the process. For example, while you do not deliberately “print” your breakfast experience, you may recall what you ate this morning. Emotional experiences are more likely to remain in memory without hard-won coding (Dolan, 2002), such as an angry quarrel with colleagues.

p29.original: 另一方面，对于概念的记忆（如心理学的基本原理），你通常需要经过深思熟虑的努力编码才能建立可用的记忆。在一个所谓精细化的过程中，你会试图将新概念与记忆中已有的信息联系起来。一种方式是将新的概念与个人化的具体例子相联系。例如，当你在记忆负强化（negative reinforcement）这一概念时将之与服用阿司匹林消除疼痛的经历联系起来。（为了便于你进行精细化加工，本文特意提供了许多这样的例子，我们希望这些例子能够帮助你将新的概念与自己的经历相联系。）事实上，没有成功进行精细化是导致记忆出现错误的一种常见原因：例如，如果你不知道1美分硬币测试的答案，可能是因为你从来没有密切关注过硬币的外形，所以你从一开始就没有对它进行真正的编码。
p29.en: On the other hand, for the memory of concepts (e.g. the philosophy of psychology), you usually need a well-thought-out effort code to create the available memory. In a process of so-called fine-tuning, you will try to link new concepts to the information that is already available in your memory. One way is to link new concepts to specific examples of individualization. For example, when you're using the concept of negative memory enhancement, it is linked to the experience of using aspirin to remove pain. (In order to facilitate your fine-tuning, this paper offers many examples, which we hope will help you to link new concepts to your own experience. In fact, the lack of successful refinement is a common cause of memory errors: if, for example, you don't know the answer to the one cent coin test, you probably didn't really code it from the start because you never paid close attention to its appearance.

p30.original: 2. 存储（storage）是记忆的第二项基本任务，它是指将已编码的信息进行长期保存的过程。但这个过程并不简单。随着对记忆工作机制的深入了解，你会发现记忆由三个部分或阶段组成，每个阶段都以不同的时长和不同的形式存储记忆。长期存储难以记忆的材料的诀窍就是及时按照长时记忆“喜欢”的方式重新对信息进行编码。例如，在听讲座时，在新信息出现与旧信息遗失之前，你可能只有几秒钟的时间对教授声音中蕴含的模式或意义进行编码（如察觉她使用了“编码”这个术语）。
p30.en: Storage (storage) is the second essential task of memory, which refers to the long-term preservation of coded information. But the process is not simple. As memory work becomes better understood, you find that memory consists of three parts or stages, each of which is stored over different periods and in different forms. The trick of long-term storage of hard-to-remember material is to recode the information in a timely manner in a long-term memory “like”. For example, when listening to a lecture, you may have only a few seconds to encode the pattern or meaning inherent in the professor's voice (e.g., when she is aware that she uses the term “coding”).

p31.original: 3. 提取（retrieval）是记忆的第三项基本任务，它是对你前期努力编码和存储信息的回报。当你拥有正确编码的记忆时，在一个有利线索的提示下，你只需要一瞬间就可以获得相关信息并使其进入意识层面；或者在特定情况下，这些信息会无意识地影响你的行为。（让我们来测试一下你的有意识提取能力：你能想起三项基本记忆任务中哪一个发生在“存储”之前吗？）
p31.en: 3. The extraction (retriev) is the third essential task of memory, which is the return to your earlier efforts to encode and store information. When you have the memory of the correct code, you need only a moment to get the information and get it to the level of consciousness, at the hint of a favourable clue; Or, in certain circumstances, this information will inadvertently affect your behaviour. (Let's test your conscious extraction: Can you remember which of the three basic memory missions happened before "storage"? I don't think so.

p32.original: 唉，记忆的提取并不总是准确的，虽然人类的记忆系统确实不一般，但它有时会出错，会扭曲信息，甚至会让我们感到失望。好消息是你可以通过一些简单的技巧来克服我们记忆中的许多常见错误，我们将在本章的后续内容中讨论这些技巧。
p32.en: Alas, the extraction of memory is not always accurate, and although the human memory system is indeed remarkable, it sometimes makes mistakes, distorts information and even disappoints us. The good news is that you can overcome many common errors in our memory through some simple techniques that we will discuss in the follow-up to this chapter.

p33.original: 心理学很有用 你想拥有“摄影式记忆”吗
p33.en: Psychology is useful. You want to have photographic memory?

p34.original: 假设你的记忆十分生动和准确，使得你可以在下次考试时从记忆中“读取”这本书的某一个段落。查尔斯·斯特罗迈耶（Charles Stromeyer）和约瑟夫·普索特卡（Joseph Psotka）测试的一位23岁的女性便具备这项能力（Stromeyer & Psotka，1970）。她能做到的最不可思议的事就是能够观察图5-2中左边图案中毫无意义的点阵布局，并在心里把它与右边的图像结合起来。最终形成如图5-3所示的组合模式。拥有这样的摄影式记忆不是一件好事吗？事实证明，结果并非完全如此。
p34.en: Let's say your memory is very vivid and accurate, so you can read one of the paragraphs of this book from the next test. A 23-year-old female tested by Charles Stromeyer and Joseph Psotka has this ability (Stromeyer & Psotka, 1970). The most incredible thing she could do was to be able to observe the meaningless dot pattern of the left-hand drawings in figure 5-2 and to combine it with the image on the right in her heart. This resulted in a combination model as shown in figures 5-3. Isn't it a good thing to have a photographic memory like this? This has not proved to be the case.

p36.original: 注：具有良好遗觉象的人能够在心里将这两幅图像组合起来，然后看到任何单一图像上并不会出现的东西。
p36.en: Note: People with a good legacy are able to combine the two images in their hearts and then see what does not appear on any single image.

p37.original: 请在短时间内观察图5-2左图中的点阵模式，并尝试记住它。你将左图记在脑海中后，再将目光移至右侧图片。当你看着第二个点阵时，通过回忆第一个点阵，试着将两组点阵组合在一起。如果你是极少数能在脑海中将这两种点阵模式结合起来的人，你就会看到一些在任何单一图像中都没有出现的东西。你觉得这么做有困难吗？
p37.en: Please observe the dot pattern in the left chart of figures 5-2 at short notice and try to remember it. You put the left image in your head and then you move the look to the right. When you look at the second dot, you try to combine the two sets by remembering the first dot. If you're a very few people who can combine these two dot patterns in your head, you'll see something that doesn't appear in any single image. Do you find it difficult to do that?

p38.original: 如果你有遗觉象这项能力，这对你来说就没有问题，但对大多数人来说，这是不可能的。如果你无法在记忆中组合这两张图片的内容，但是想要看到组合后的图形，请参见图5-3。
p38.en: If you have a legacy of that ability, it will be okay for you, but it will not be possible for most people. If you cannot combine the contents of the two images in your memory, see figure 5-3 for a combination.

p39.original: 图5-3 图5-2中的图形组合形成了数字的形状
p39.en: Figure 5-3. The shape of the figure in the graphic combination in Figure 5-2.

p41.original: “摄影式记忆”的专业术语是遗觉象（eidetic imagery）。心理学家更喜欢使用这个术语来指代这种现象，因为遗觉象在许多重要方面不同于摄影图像（Haber，1969，1980；Searleman，2007）。例如，一幅摄影图像能记录所有微小的细节，而一幅遗觉象则能最准确地描绘出场景中最有趣和最有意义的部分，而且遗觉象也会像“正常”记忆那样存在记忆扭曲。
p41.en: The specialized term “photographic memory” is eidetic image. Psychologists prefer the term to refer to this phenomenon, as the legacy is different from photographic images in many important respects (Haber, 1969, 1980); Saarleman, 2007. For example, a photographic image can record all the small details, while a legacy can most accurately depict the most interesting and meaningful parts of the scene, and memory can be distorted as if it were a “normal” memory.

p42.original: 遗觉记忆也在以下几个方面不同于典型的人类记忆图像。一方面，拥有遗觉象的人描述他们的记忆图像具有原始经验的生动性（Neisser，1967）。另一方面，遗觉象被想象成位于“大脑之外”而非脑海之内，它不是通过“心灵的眼睛”看到的。（然而，与产生幻觉的人不同，拥有遗觉象的人会将这些图像看作心理表象。）此外，在某些情况下，遗觉象可以持续几分钟甚至几天之久。例如，对于斯特罗迈耶和普索特卡测试的那名女性而言，即使她看到两个图像的时间相隔24小时，她仍能将其中的点进行组合并通过测试。但值得注意的是，持续存在的遗觉象可能是一种坏事。拥有遗觉象的人们报告说，这种生动的图像有时会扰乱他们的思维，干扰他们对其他事情的思考（Hunter，1964）。
p42.en: The memory is also different from typical images of human memory in several respects. On the one hand, people with a legacy describe the vividness of their memory images with their original experience (Neisser, 1967). On the other hand, it is imagined to be “outside the brain” rather than inside the brain, and it is not seen through the “eyes of the heart”. (However, unlike those who produce hallucinations, those who have a legacy view these images as psychological manifestations. In addition, in some cases, it can last for a few minutes or even days. For example, for the woman tested in Stromier and Pusotka, even if she saw the two images 24 hours apart, she was able to combine and test their points. It is worth noting, however, that the persistence of a legacy may be a bad thing. People with a legacy report that such vivid images sometimes disrupt their thinking and their thinking about other things (Hunter, 1964).

p43.original: 遗觉象在儿童中最为常见，而极少发生在成年人身上。一项研究估计，多达5%的儿童表现出一些遗觉象能力，尽管在大多数情况下，这种能力还不足以帮助他们通过“点阵组合测试”（Gray & Gummerman，1975）。而且，遗觉象记忆不存在性别差异：男孩和女孩拥有这种能力的可能性相近（Searleman，2007）。虽然没有人知道为什么遗觉象的能力会在成年期消失，但它可能遵循着某种发展序列，就像儿童的乳牙在成长中会脱落一样。遗觉象能力的消失可能与人们开始强调逻辑思维有关，一般伴随着正规教育的开始，并跟随儿童思维方式的变化而变化。
p43.en: The legacy is most common among children and rarely occurs among adults. A study estimates that as many as 5 per cent of children show some legacy capacity, although in most cases this capacity is not sufficient to help them pass the “point-form test” (Gray & Gummerman, 1975). Moreover, there is no gender difference in memory: boys and girls are more likely to have this ability (Searleman, 2007). While no one knows why the ability of the legacy disappears in adulthood, it may follow a certain sequence of development, just as the child's breast teeth will fall out of growth. The disappearance of memory capacity may be associated with the beginning of emphasis on logic thinking, which is usually accompanied by the beginning of formal education and changes in the way children think.

p44.original: 个案研究还表明，遗觉象的消退与语言技能的发展之间存在联系：拥有遗觉象的人报告说，当他们仅仅关注图像时，遗觉象是最强的；当用词语描述遗觉象时，会使其从记忆中消退，而拥有遗觉象的人可以学会利用这个事实来控制遗觉象对他们的干扰（Haber，1969，1970）。司法心理学的研究表明，对于普通人（非拥有遗觉象的人）来说，用语言描述嫌疑人的面孔也会干扰他们随后对这些面孔的记忆。同样，试图用语言描述其他难以口头表达的知觉刺激，如某种声音或葡萄酒的味道，也会削弱大多数人描述后再去回忆这些知觉刺激的能力（Bower，2003；Dodson et al.，1997）。
p44.en: The case studies also show that there is a link between the loss of a legacy and the development of language skills: people who have a legacy report that when they focus only on images, they are the strongest; When it is depicted in words, it fades away from memory, and those who have it can learn to use it to control interference with it (Haber, 1969, 1970). Studies of judicial psychology have shown that for ordinary people (other than those who have a legacy), the description of a suspect's face in language can also interfere with their subsequent memory of those faces. Similarly, attempts to describe in language other sensory irritations that are difficult to express orally, such as a certain sound or the taste of wine, can reduce the ability of most people to describe them and then remember them (Bower, 2003); Dodson et al., 1997.

p45.original: 尼日利亚的一项研究进一步支持了上述观点，语言技能和视觉表象之间的冲突可能导致遗觉象能力的丧失：遗觉象不仅在伊博族儿童中很常见，而且在乡村的文盲中也很常见。尽管这些部落里的许多成年人都能够正确地绘制出先前看到的图像的细节，但同一部落里搬到城市并学会了阅读的成员就几乎没有遗觉象能力（Doob，1964）。
p45.en: This view is further supported by a study in Nigeria, where conflicts between language skills and visual appearances can lead to the loss of memory capacity: it is common not only among Ibo children, but also in rural illiteracy. Although many adults in these tribes were able to draw the details of previously seen images correctly, members of the same tribe who moved to the city and learned to read had little memory capacity (Doob, 1964).

p46.original: 不管遗觉象记忆是什么，它显然都是非常罕见的能力。事实上，遗觉象罕见到一些心理学家都在质疑它的存在（Crowder，1992）。正如我们所看到的，现有的几项关于“摄像式记忆”的研究都把它描绘成不同于日常记忆的能力。然而，事实是我们对这种现象仍知之甚少，目前也少有心理学家对其进行研究。
p46.en: Whatever the memory, it is clearly a very rare ability. In fact, it is rare for some psychologists to question its existence (Crowder, 1992). As we have seen, several existing studies on “photo-memory” portray it as distinct from the ability of everyday memory. However, the fact remains that we still have little knowledge of the phenomenon and that there are few psychologists who study it.

p47.original: 遗觉象不仅对那些拥有它的个体来说是一个现实问题，而且对认知心理学家来说也是一个理论问题。一方面，如果遗觉象真的存在，那么它是否是我们已知的记忆成分在其中发挥作用的结果？另一方面，如果它被证明是一种独特的记忆形式，那么我们又如何用被普遍接受的记忆三阶段模型解释它呢？
p47.en: The legacy is not only a real problem for those who own it, but also a theoretical one for cognitive psychologists. On the one hand, if the legacy really exists, is it the result of the functioning of what is known to be our memory component? On the other hand, if it has proved to be a unique form of memory, how can we interpret it with a universally accepted three-stage memory model?
